fix_assessment.rationale: Consolidate the explicit signer-rejection evidence with issue 50795; do not claim every timeout has the same cause or recommend disabling verification.

judgment.recommended_action: Consolidate the explicit signer-rejection evidence with issue 50795; do not claim every timeout has the same cause or recommend disabling verification.
evidence: The original report documents pairing timeout despite firewall, network, key and restart checks; later comments confirm affected 0.102.3001 installations.
A commenter explicitly supplies Rejected Settings IPC client: untrusted-signature. Other comments are symptom-only and must not automatically inherit that diagnosis.
Read all current comments, including the latest rollback report, and primary issue 50795 with its current-release signer inventories.
NamedPipePeerVerification rejects a peer when MeetsSigningPolicy fails; this can prevent Settings from reaching MWB regardless of firewall changes.
The service-removal observation is not a controlled fix and does not establish a second cause or a shipped correction.

The latest reporter says reverting to 0.101 works, while restarting both systems and clearing MWB local state did not. This supports a version regression but does not identify that reporter's signer-verification result.

A new commenter reports that replacing the three MWB launcher executables with files from another release restored pairing on two x64 machine-wide installations: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/51567#issuecomment-6482766769

This is an unofficial mixed-version workaround reported by one commenter, not independently validated, a shipped fix, or evidence covering other architectures/install scopes. A Settings executable swap reportedly caused a runner version mismatch.
judgment.rationale: There is already primary tracking for the confirmed rejection. A second competing trust-policy design here would duplicate work and risk conflating symptom-only cases. Preserve primary tracking in #50795. Do not present cross-release file replacement as an approved correction or weaken signer/version checks.

comment.body: Thanks for the signer analysis and the new two-machine result. That result adds useful evidence for the rejection already tracked in #50795, but it covers an unofficial mixture of 0.102 and 0.103 executables on x64 machine-wide installs, not a validated release fix. Please keep this evidence with #50795. The reported runner version-mismatch after swapping Settings also means that replacing arbitrary components is not a general workaround. Reports with only the same pairing message still need the exact failure-time rejection before being assigned this cause; no signature-verification bypass is proposed.
